contributions.statement: Do not accept a skill- or mapping-file-assisted Java framework migration on compile or deploy success; gate it on containerized behavioral tests, because framework-pair skill bundles raised compile and deploy rates (e.g. Gemini deploy 7% to 61%) while barely moving, and for one agent lowering, behavioral test pass.
contributions.evidence: §5.1 Table 2, App. E.3, Tables 7-8: skills vs monolithic prompt across 5 CLI agents and 204 directed Spring/Jakarta EE/Quarkus tasks; staged compile->deploy->test oracle with 1,331 expert tests. Single run per task; skills written by the benchmark authors.
relative_to: 2607.25333 skills without execution feedback gave no gain

contributions.statement: Treat cross-framework migration of enterprise Java (Spring <-> Jakarta EE <-> Quarkus) as beyond autonomous agent reach today: scope agents to sub-steps behind a compile->deploy->behavioral-test gate per step, since the best agent passed ~15% of behavioral tests and only 1 of 204 tasks came out fully equivalent (Jakarta EE target: 2% pass, 57% compile failures).
contributions.evidence: §5 Table 2 (15.3% focused, 12.2% whole-app aggregate test pass), §5.1 Fig. 3 (per-target framework), App. C (1/204 fully equivalent). Single runs, contamination acknowledged.
relative_to: 2607.17957 DepBench same-framework dependency upgrades (e.g. Spring Boot 2.7->3.0)

reason: On the team's own stack, it shows that skills move migrations to 'runnable' but not 'correct', and it gives a hard capability ceiling for framework migration. The failure taxonomy (config/DI wiring) is LLM-annotated and weak, so it is not used.
